(OIML Issuing Authority NL1) - Address: Thijssweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, The Netherlands - Person responsible: M.Ph.D. Schmidt - Phone: +31 88 6362332 - Email: certin@nmi.nl - Website: www.nmi.nl - OIML issuer ID: NL1 Applicant and Manufacturer: - Mettler-Toledo GmbH - Im Langacher 44, CH-8606 Greifensee, Switzerland Certified type: - Category: Indicator - Type: IND360 Recommendation: - R76, edition 2006, scheme A, accuracy classes: I, II, III, IIII (the certificate says "for accuracy class (I) or (II) or (III) or (IIII)") Test reports: - NMi-2493052-01, revision 1, 2021-03-01, 56 pages, type_evaluation_report - NMi-2493052-02, revision 1, 2021-03-01, 15 pages, type_evaluation_report - NMi-2493052-03, revision 1, 2021-03-01, 21 pages, type_evaluation_report - NMi-2493052-04, revision 1, 2021-03-01, 20 pages, type_evaluation_report - NMi-2659880-01, 2021-10-27, 24 pages, type_evaluation_report (or evaluation_report) Actually, "OIML Type Evaluation Reports" — all are type evaluation reports. The last one might be the evaluation report for the current project. I'll label all as type_evaluation_report. Hmm, but the date 29 October 2021 — the first four were revised (revision 1 dated 1 March 2021), the last NMi-2659880-01 dated 27 October 2021 matches the project number. I'll mark them all type_evaluation_report. Revision history: - Initial, 2020-12-24, Initial issue - 1, 2021-03-02, Type evaluation reports revised because of editorial changes - 2, 2021-09-15, Editorial change to include DC power supply voltage for all versions - 3, 2021-10-29, Adding optional ISB (Intrinsic safety barrier) Now the characteristics. Page 2 table: Digital load cells or Weighing modules — two configuration variants: 1. CANbus interface 2. SICSPro interface For CANbus interface: - Accuracy class OIML R 76: (III) or (IIII) - OIML R 51: Y(a) or Y(b); XIII(x) or XIII(2) — this is odd, "XIII(x)" is probably "X(1)"... wait, actually R51 accuracy classes are X, Y, Z. "XIII(x)" might be OCR of "X(1)" or similar. Let me keep as given: "Y(a) or Y(b)" and "XIII(x) or XIII(2)". Hmm, actually it might be "X(1), Y(1)..." Not sure. I'll keep the values as they appear. Actually wait — R51 classes: Y(a), Y(b), Z... The "XIII(x)" is likely OCR garble of "X(1)" or "XII(x)"? The SICSPro column says "XI(x), XII(x), XIII(x) or XIII(2)" — these look like class designations for R51. Actually R51 automatic catchweighing instruments classes are X, Y, Z with factors (1), (2)... The marking is like "XI(1)" etc. Hmm, for R51 the classes are XI, XII, XIII for class X with special factors, YI...Y(b), Z. Actually yes! R51 classes: X(I), XII... Let me recall: OIML R 51 classes are XI, XII, XIII (for class X instruments with interval factors), YI, YII, YIII? No... R51: Class X, Y, Z; with subdivision: XI(1), XI(2), XII(1)... Hmm. Actually in R51, accuracy class X instruments are marked XI(1), XII(1), XIII(1), XI(2), etc. where Roman numeral is the number of scale intervals exponent and the parenthetical is the verification scale interval factor. Class Y: Y(a), Y(b). Class Z: Z. So "XIII(x) or XIII(2)" — x might be OCR for "1"? And "XI(x), XII(x), XIII(x) or XIII(2)" — hmm. I'll keep values as strings as given in the markdown, since I shouldn't fabricate. Keep "Y(a) or Y(b), XIII(x) or XIII(2)" as given. Actually the values are per interface configuration, so this could be a config_level entry: attribute "accuracy_class_oiml_r51", axis "interface", values: [{condition: "CANbus interface", value: "Y(a) or Y(b) / XIII(x) or XIII(2)"}, {condition: "SICSPro interface", value: "Y(I), Y(II), Y(a) or Y(b) / XI(x), XII(x), XIII(x) or XIII(2)"}]. Hmm wait — "Y(I), Y(II), Y(a) or Y(b)" — that looks garbled too (maybe "Y(1), Y(2), Y(a) or Y(b)"). I'll keep as-is. - OIML R 61: Ref(0,2) — both columns. This is R61 (automatic gravimetric filling) "Ref(0,2)" — probably "Ref (0,2)" accuracy/referee? Keep as string "Ref(0.2)"? Rule says decimal separator conversions apply to numbers. "Ref(0,2)" is a designation; I could keep as "Ref(0,2)" since it's an identifier, not a numeric value. Hmm, rule 2 says convert European decimals. But this is a class designation. I'll keep "Ref(0.2)"? Actually, I think it's safer to keep the designation as-is: "Ref(0,2)". It's not a measurement value. I'll keep "Ref(0,2)". - Weighing ranges: CANbus: Single interval; SICSPro: Single interval, Multi-interval, Multiple range - Max number of scale intervals (one weighing range): n ≤ 10000 divisions vs n ≤ 1000000 divisions - Max number of scale intervals (multi-interval or multiple range): "-" (CANbus, i.e., not applicable) vs n ≤ 100000 divisions (per (partial) weighing range) - Max number of weighing ranges: 1 vs 3 - Load cell power supply: 12 V DC (both) - Fraction of maximum permissible error: 0 (both) — p factor? For indicators (digital), p = 0? Interesting. Keep value 0. - Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C (both) - Humidity: non-condensing - Intended location: Closed - Electromagnetic environment class: E2 - Power supply voltage: 100–240 V AC 50-60 Hz (only for Harsh version), 20-28 V DC (for all versions), not suitable for road vehicle power supply. Page 3 table: Analog load cells vs Analog load cells with ISB (Intrinsic Safety Barrier) — three columns: "Analog load cells" (1 col), "Analog load cells with ISB" (3 cols). Wait: ``` Analog load cellsAnalog load cells with ISB ``` So columns: Analog load cells; Analog load cells with ISB (3 sub-columns). - Accuracy class OIML R 76: (III) or (IIII) — colspan 4 (both) - OIML R 51: Y(a) or Y(b); XIII(x) or XIII(2) — colspan 4 - OIML R 61: Ref(0,2) — colspan 4 - Weighing range(s): Single interval — colspan 4 - Max number of scale intervals: n ≤ 10000 divisions (Analog), n ≤ 10000 divisions (with ISB) — same - Minimum signal input voltage: Umin = 0 mV both - Minimum input voltage per verification scale interval: 0.3 µV (Analog) vs 0.25 µV (with ISB) - Load cell excitation voltage: 5 V DC (Analog); with ISB: 1.5 V DC, 2.3 V DC, 3.9 V DC (three sub-columns) - Minimum load cell resistance: 43 Ω (Analog); with ISB: 43 Ω, 87 Ω, 350 Ω - Maximum load cell resistance: 1245 Ω (both/all) - Fraction of max permissible error: 0.5 - Load cell connection: 6-wire (remote sensing) - Max value of cable length per cross wire section...: 1571 m/mm² - Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C - Humidity: non-condensing; location: Closed - EM environment class: E2 - Power supply voltage: same as page 2. Hmm, the "with ISB" three sub-columns: these correspond to different excitation voltages (1.5, 2.3, 3.9 V DC) and matching minimum load cell resistances (43, 87, 350 Ω). Interesting: min resistance pairs with excitation voltage. Actually for ISB, higher excitation → higher min resistance? 1.5V→43Ω, 2.3V→87Ω, 3.9V→350Ω. So this is a configuration matrix. The ISB variants have 3 configurations. I could model this as config_level entries with two axes, or as a matrix_table. Approach: Use config_level for indicator page 2 (axis: interface: CANbus vs SICSPro) and page 3 (axis: load cell connection type: analog vs analog with ISB). But the ISB column has 3 sub-configurations. Maybe model as: config_level entries: - attribute: minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval, axis: load_cell_interface, values: [{condition: "Analog load cells", value: 0.3, unit_symbol: "µV"}, {condition: "Analog load cells with ISB", value: 0.25, unit_symbol: "µV"}] - attribute: load_cell_excitation_voltage, axis: load_cell_interface, values: [{condition: "Analog load cells", value: 5, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "Analog load cells with ISB (config 1)", value: 1.5, unit_symbol: "V"}, ...] Hmm, that's getting complicated. Better to also include matrix_tables to preserve the raw structure. Let me structure: matrix_tables: 1. name: "Characteristics of the indicator / terminal — Digital load cells or weighing modules", columns: ["attribute", "canbus_interface", "sicspro_interface"], rows: list of attribute rows. Actually matrix_tables schema: name, columns[], rows[] (object per row), description, footnotes[]. For page 2 table: columns = ["attribute", "canbus_interface", "sicspro_interface"], rows = [{"attribute": "Accuracy class (OIML R 76)", "canbus_interface": "(III) or (IIII)", "sicspro_interface": "(I), (II), (III) or (IIII)"}, ...]. 2. name: "Characteristics — Analog load cells vs Analog load cells with ISB", columns: ["attribute", "analog_load_cells", "analog_load_cells_with_isb_1", "analog_load_cells_with_isb_2", "analog_load_cells_with_isb_3"]... Hmm, or keep two columns and note the ISB has 3 sub-columns. Since excitation voltage and min resistance vary across the 3 ISB sub-columns, I'll represent ISB configs as three variants with excitation/resistance pairs. Actually let me reconsider: maybe better to model ISB sub-columns as configurations within config_level with axis "load cell connection (analog with ISB) excitation option". And matrix_tables preserve both raw tables. Let me plan the JSON: ```json { "certificate": { "number": "R76/2006-A-NL1-20.70", "scheme": "A", "project_number": "2659880", "page_total": 4, "member_state": "The Netherlands", "date_issued": "2021-10-29", "oiml_issuer_id": "NL1" }, "issuing_authority": { "name": "NMi Certin B.V.", "address_lines": ["Thijssweg 11", "2629 JA Delft", "The Netherlands"], "person_responsible": "M.Ph.D. Schmidt", "phone": "+31 88 6362332", "email": "certin@nmi.nl", "website": "www.nmi.nl", "oiml_issuer_id": "NL1" }, "applicants": [ { "name": "Mettler-Toledo GmbH", "address_lines": ["Im Langacher 44", "CH-8606 Greifensee", "Switzerland"] } ], "manufacturers": [ { "name": "Mettler-Toledo GmbH", "address_lines": ["Im Langacher 44", "CH-8606 Greifensee", "Switzerland"] } ], "certified_type": { "category": "Indicator", "type_designations": ["IND360"], "module_designation": null, "description": "Indicator / Terminal" }, "recommendation": { "id": "R76", "edition": 2006, "scheme": "A", "accuracy_classes": ["I", "II", "III", "IIII"] }, "test_reports": [...], "revision_history": [...], ... } ``` Also R51 and R61 are mentioned as additional recommendations the type conforms to. The schema has single `recommendation` object. Hmm. The primary recommendation is R 76. R51 and R61 mentions are about accuracy classes under those recommendations for use in those instrument types (the indicator can be used in R51/R61 instruments). I'll keep the primary recommendation as R76. Maybe add additional conformances in matrix or characteristics? The schema doesn't have a place for multiple recommendations. I could note them in characteristics as type_level strings. That seems reasonable: `applicable_recommendations_r51_classes` etc. Actually better to keep them in the matrix tables and config_level as attributes. Now characteristics: type_level (whole-cert, applies to all configs): - temperature_range: {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C - climatic_environment_humidity: "non-condensing" - intended_location: "Closed" - electromagnetic_environment_class: "E2" - load_cell_power_supply: 12 V DC (this applies to page-2 table only; page 3 has excitation 5V/1.5/2.3/3.9 — different thing: load cell power supply 12 V DC is for digital load cells/weighing modules interface; analog load cells use excitation voltage from indicator). Hmm. Load cell power supply 12 V DC appears in page 2 table (digital load cells / weighing modules). Page 3 (analog) doesn't have it. So it's config-scoped really. But it's colspan=2 across both CANbus and SICSPro columns. I'll put it in config_level with axis "interface" and both conditions, or type_level with note. Hmm. Actually, let me define configuration axes: Axis 1 (page 2): interface: "CANbus interface" (digital load cells) vs "SICSPro interface" (digital weighing modules / precision) Axis 2 (page 3): analog connection: "Analog load cells" vs "Analog load cells with ISB" (3 excitation options) config_level entries (axis: "interface"): 1. attribute: accuracy_class_oiml_r76, axis: interface, values: [{condition: "CANbus interface", value: "(III) or (IIII)"}, {condition: "SICSPro interface", value: "(I), (II), (III) or (IIII)"}] 2. attribute: accuracy_class_oiml_r51, axis: interface, values: [{condition: "CANbus interface", value: "Y(a) or Y(b); XIII(x) or XIII(2)"}, {condition: "SICSPro interface", value: "Y(I), Y(II), Y(a) or Y(b); XI(x), XII(x), XIII(x) or XIII(2)"}] 3. attribute: accuracy_class_oiml_r61, axis: interface, values: both "Ref(0,2)" 4. attribute: weighing_ranges, axis: interface, values: [{condition: "CANbus interface", value: "Single interval"}, {condition: "SICSPro interface", value: "Single interval, Multi-interval, Multiple range"}] 5. attribute: max_scale_intervals_single_range, axis: interface, values: [{CANbus: 10000, unit "divisions"}, {SICSPro: 1000000, unit "divisions"}] 6. attribute: max_scale_intervals_multi_interval_or_multiple_range, axis: interface, values: [{CANbus: null (not applicable)}, {SICSPro: 100000, unit "divisions", note "per (partial) weighing range"}] 7. attribute: max_number_of_weighing_ranges, axis: interface, values: [{CANbus: 1}, {SICSPro: 3}] 8. attribute: load_cell_power_supply, axis: interface, values: [{CANbus: 12 V DC}, {SICSPro: 12 V DC}] config_level entries (axis: "load_cell_connection"): 1. attribute: accuracy_class_oiml_r76, axis: load_cell_connection, values: [{Analog: "(III) or (IIII)"}, {ISB: "(III) or (IIII)"}] — same for both; maybe type_level instead. Since both analog tables share R76 class (III)/(IIII) and R51/R61 etc., these could be type_level. But they differ from page-2 SICSPro (I),(II). Hmm — page 2 and page 3 are different connection families (digital vs analog). The R76 accuracy class overall certificate covers (I)-(IIII) for the indicator; specific configurations limit it. This is getting complex. Simplify: keep page-2 attributes under axis "interface" and page-3 attributes under axis "load_cell_connection". Common attributes (temperature, humidity, location, EMC, power supply voltage) go type_level. Page-3 config_level (axis: load_cell_connection): 1. maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: [{condition: "Analog load cells", value: {min:null, max:10000}, unit: "divisions"}, {condition: "Analog load cells with ISB", value: {max: 10000}}] 2. minimum_signal_input_voltage: both "Umin = 0 mV" → value 0, unit mV. Represent as {value: {min:null, max:0}, unit_symbol: "mV"}? "Umin = 0 mV" means minimum input voltage is 0 mV → value 0, unit mV. I'll do {value: 0, unit_symbol: "mV"} with attribute name minimum_signal_input_voltage_umin. Keep string "Umin = 0 mV"? Better structured: attribute "minimum_signal_input_voltage_umin": value 0, unit mV. 3. minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval: [{Analog: 0.3 µV}, {ISB: 0.25 µV}] 4. load_cell_excitation_voltage: [{Analog: 5 V DC}, {ISB config A: 1.5 V}, {ISB config B: 2.3 V}, {ISB config C: 3.9 V}]. Conditions: "Analog load cells", "Analog load cells with ISB (43 Ω min load cell resistance)", "Analog load cells with ISB (87 Ω min)", "Analog load cells with ISB (350 Ω min)". Hmm, or condition "Analog load cells with ISB - option 1/2/3". 5. minimum_load_cell_resistance: [{Analog: 43 Ω}, {ISB option1: 43 Ω}, {ISB option2: 87 Ω}, {ISB option3: 350 Ω}] 6. maximum_load_cell_resistance: 1245 Ω (both) → type_level? It's within the analog axis. I'll put config_level with both conditions, or type_level. It appears colspan=4 (all analog columns). But is it also for digital? The page-3 table only covers analog. Since the whole cert includes digital too, I'd scope it to axis load_cell_connection. I'll include both conditions. type_level: - temperature_range: {min:-10, max:40} °C - humidity: "non-condensing" - intended_location: "Closed" - electromagnetic_environment_class: "E2" - power_supply_voltage: handled with splits: - power_supply_voltage_ac: {min:100, max:240} V (only for Harsh version) - power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz - power_supply_voltage_dc: {min:20, max:28} V (for all versions) - note: not suitable for road vehicle power supply → maybe a characteristic power_supply_road_vehicle_suitable: false or a note. I'll add `power_supply_notes` as a string? Schema values must be structured. I can add attribute "power_supply_type": "AC or DC". And maybe skip road vehicle note or include as footnote-like. There's no footnote marker in the doc for that; it's parenthetical text. I'll include attribute "power_supply_road_vehicle_suitable": {value: false}. Hmm — fabrication? The text says "(not suitable for a road vehicle power supply)" so value false is faithful. I'll include it. - fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error (p_ind / plc-ish): page 2: 0 (digital); page 3: 0.5 (analog). So it's config-scoped! Axis: indicator_connection_family. I'll do config_level with axis "connection family" conditions: "Digital load cells or weighing modules" value 0; "Analog load cells (with or without ISB)" value 0.5. Value 0 dimensionless... "Fraction of the maximum permissible error" = 0 for digital? That seems odd but as printed. Keep value 0 and 0.5, unit null. - load_cell_connection: "6-wire (remote sensing)" — analog table only. config_level axis load_cell_connection both conditions, or type_level? It's in analog table only. Put in config_level with both analog conditions. - maximum_cable_length_per_cross_section: 1571 m/mm² — attribute "max_cable_length_per_cross_wire_section": value 1571, unit "m/mm²". Analog table only. - weighing_range(s) for analog: Single interval — config_level. Now, digital table attributes scoped to interface axis. Let me also record R51/R61 class entries. Software identification table: - Analog mainboard: 1.xx.yyyy - POWERCELL mainboard: 1.xx.yyyy (CANbus interface) - Precision mainboard: 1.xx.yyyy (SICSPro interface) These are software components. Could be components[] with role "software"? The schema components role/type_designations. Maybe add to matrix_tables as "Software identification" table, and/or components with role "firmware". I'll add a matrix_table for software identification and mention in description. I could add components entries: components: - {role: "digital load cell interface (CANbus)", type_designations: ["POWERCELL mainboard"], characteristics: {firmware_version: "1.xx.yyyy"}} Hmm, the mainboards are firmware, not hardware components. I'll record them as matrix_table only, plus maybe components with role "software". Let me add them as components with role "Software (mainboard firmware)": components[]: 1. {role: "Software — mainboard", type_designations: ["Analog mainboard"], characteristics: {"version": {value: "1.xx.yyyy"}}} 2. {role: "Software — mainboard (CANbus interface)", type_designations: ["POWERCELL mainboard"], ...} 3. {role: "Software — mainboard (SICSPro interface)", type_designations: ["Precision mainboard"], ...} And footnote about xx/yyyy meaning. The explanation "(xx is a number between 00 and 99 ... yyyy ... between 0000 and 9999 ...)" can be a footnote with marker null? Footnotes have marker/text. I can use marker "note" or omit. Schema: footnotes[]: marker, text. I could add marker "*" with that text. Hmm, fabricating a marker is iffy. I'll add footnote marker "(xx)"? Eh. Maybe better: include the explanation in the matrix_table description. So column names could be generic: "analog_load_cells", "analog_with_isb_config_1", "analog_with_isb_config_2", "analog_with_isb_config_3". Rows preserve raw strings.
